title: TestIdentity
description: A synthetic principal the target establishes in its evaluation environment so an agent can act as a known user or service during evaluation (spec §8.2). Returned by GET /aep/identities and GET /aep/identities/{identityId}, with applicability computed for the calling identity (AEP-REQ-141). Evaluators discover identities and bind one at session start by identityId; they never create them and never receive the identity's credentials (AEP-REQ-145). The document is descriptive: additionalProperties is false so no credential-shaped field can be added, 'attributes' rejects credential-like property names, and its values MUST NOT carry secrets or real PII (AEP-REQ-144). This file also hosts the agent-side declaration, $defs/IdentityModel, referenced by AgentContract.contextModel.identity and AgentSummary.identityBinding so the two cannot drift.

identityId.description: Stable handle the evaluator passes as identityId at session start. Possession confers nothing: binding is authorized against the caller's own credential (AEP-REQ-145), so this need not be high-entropy and MAY be human-readable. Retired identities keep their id so Trace snapshots resolve (AEP-REQ-141).

description.description: What this identity is for: its role, what seeded data it can see, what it cannot do. Evaluators choose identities from this text.

roles.description: Product-defined role labels the identity holds (e.g. 'admin', 'viewer'). Descriptive; the product's authorization layer remains authoritative.

attributes.description: Descriptive, non-secret attributes evaluators may filter or reason on (locale, seniority, plan tier, feature flags). Property names that look like credentials (token, secret, passw*, credential, cookie, api key, private key, bearer, session id) fail the schema; values MUST NOT contain credentials or real personally identifiable information either, which only contract validation can check (AEP-REQ-144, AEP-REQ-145).

applicability.description: Per-caller projection of where this identity may be bound (AEP-REQ-141): one entry per agent the CALLING IDENTITY may bind it to, with the live modes in which it may do so. Computed as the intersection of the target's declared applicability, the agent's evaluationModes, and the caller's per-agent per-mode authorization, so an entry never names an agent the caller cannot see and never lists a mode the agent lacks. Entries MUST have distinct agentIds. The target's declaration itself (wildcards and all) is not on the wire. An identity with no entries for a caller is omitted from that caller's list.

fixture.description: Seeded state behind the identity, when its behavior depends on any. Required for identities with seeded state (AEP-REQ-150).

maxConcurrentSessions.description: How many sessions may hold this identity at once; a slot is held from created→active until the session leaves active and is enforced per fixtureId across identities that share one (AEP-REQ-150). Identities with a per-session fixture reset are typically 1.

status.description: 'available' — may be bound now. 'unavailable' — exists and is applicable but cannot be bound now (reset in progress, at concurrency limit, maintenance); binding returns -32072 with retryAfterMs. 'retired' — permanent; kept for Trace continuity and omitted from default listings (AEP-REQ-141); new bindings return -32071, which is not retryable (AEP-REQ-148 c).

availableAt.description: When an 'unavailable' identity is expected to become available, if known. Only permitted when status is 'unavailable'.

lastUpdatedAt.description: When the identity document last changed, including the transition to 'retired'. Drives the updatedSince filter (AEP-REQ-142).

IdentityKind.description: 'user' — a synthetic end-user principal. 'service' — a non-human principal (integration, automation, agent-to-agent caller). Custom kinds use reverse-DNS prefixes. Shared by TestIdentity.kind, IdentityBinding.kind and AgentContract.contextModel.identity.kinds.

tenantId.description: The isolation scope the identity belongs to, as the target defines it (tenant, organization, account, project). MUST be an evaluation scope, never a production one (AEP-REQ-086, AEP-REQ-130). Tenancy is not the isolation boundary between identities; the fixture is (AEP-REQ-150).

agentId.description: An agent the caller may bind this identity to. Its contract accepts this identity's kind (spec §8.2).

authorizedModes.description: Live modes in which the CALLING IDENTITY may bind this identity to this agent for a fresh session. 'replay' is deliberately not listable: replaying a Trace that recorded this identity is governed by the Trace's mode and AEP-REQ-046, not by this list (AEP-REQ-148 c, AEP-REQ-151). An identity whose fixture never resets never lists 'sandboxed-live' (AEP-REQ-150).

fixtureId.description: Identifies the seeded state. Identities that share state share a fixtureId; the concurrency limit is enforced per fixtureId (AEP-REQ-150).

version.description: Opaque identifier for the seeded state's content, compared for equality only — no ordering is defined. The target changes it whenever the fixture content changes (AEP-REQ-150).

digest.description: Digest over a target-defined canonical serialization of the fixture at its declared version, as last reset or verified (AEP-REQ-150). Two equal digests describe equal state.

resetPolicy.description: 'none' — fixture is never reset; such an identity is never applicable in sandboxed-live (AEP-REQ-150). 'per-session' — restored to 'version' before every binding. 'scheduled' — restored on a target-defined schedule. 'on-demand' — restored when the target chooses; the Trace snapshot records what was seen.

IdentityBinding.title: IdentityBinding
IdentityBinding.description: Snapshot of a test identity as resolved when a session bound it (AEP-REQ-149). Recorded on EvaluationSession.identity and Trace.identity, and carried whole on the session.started stream event so Trace reconstruction from the stream stays lossless (AEP-REQ-114). tenancy, roles and fixture are present whenever the bound identity carries them. Carries no credentials (AEP-REQ-145).

authorizationRef.description: Opaque, high-entropy reference (AEP-REQ-126) to the audit record of the authorization decision that permitted this binding — which evaluator credential, under which scope, at what time (AEP-REQ-090, AEP-REQ-153). Joins the snapshot to the server's audit log without putting the evaluator's credential or scope on the Trace. A re-execution replay gets a fresh one (AEP-REQ-149).

digest.description: Computed at bind time, after any per-session reset: the state the session actually started against (AEP-REQ-150).

fixture.description: Fixture version and digest as observed at bind time; re-execution replay compares against these (AEP-REQ-151).

IdentityModel.title: IdentityModel
IdentityModel.description: An agent's declaration of whether it acts as a test identity (spec §8.2, AEP-REQ-146). 'binding' is the agent-wide default; 'perMode' overrides it for individual live modes, and a mode not listed inherits 'binding'. The effective binding for a session is the value for its testMode. 'replay' is never a key: a replay follows the Trace (AEP-REQ-148 a, AEP-REQ-151). A perMode key naming a mode outside the agent's evaluationModes is a contract-validation error, not ignored (AEP-REQ-146). Mirrored unchanged on AgentSummary.identityBinding.

binding.description: Agent-wide default. 'none' — in that mode the agent's behavior is fully determined by input and injected context; identityId MUST NOT be supplied. 'optional' — the agent runs with or without a bound principal; unbound means no principal, never an ambient one. 'required' — every session in that mode MUST bind a test identity; the target MUST have declared at least one applicable identity for it (AEP-REQ-147).

perMode.description: Per-mode overrides of 'binding'. Keys are the five live modes only; values are the same three bindings. Lets an agent that runs synthetically from injected context in the lower modes declare 'none' there and 'required' in sandboxed-live, where it touches live state.

kinds.description: Identity kinds the agent can act as. Absent means any kind. Part of applicability (spec §8.2): the agent discovery filter omits identities of other kinds (AEP-REQ-142) and a bind with one is rejected with -32071 (AEP-REQ-148 c).

description.description: What the agent does with the principal: which authorization checks, which per-principal data, which attributed writes.
